content.title: About
content.content: Peanuts, honey roasted are roasted peanuts coated with a sweet honey glaze. The peanut (Arachis hypogaea) is a legume, not a true nut, cultivated in warm climates worldwide. The honey‑roasted version combines a crunchy texture, nutty flavor and a subtle sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts develop underground: after pollination the flower stalk bends down and the pod matures beneath the soil.
Honey‑roasted peanuts are popular in both Asian and American snack culture and are used in desserts and trail mixes.
Peanuts are a good source of resistant starch, which supports a healthy gut microbiome.
Honey in the glaze adds natural antimicrobial properties, extending shelf life.
In the United States honey‑roasted peanuts rank among the top‑10 best‑selling snack products.

items.title: Plant‑based protein source
items.content: Peanuts contain about 25 % protein, providing essential amino acids for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats
items.content: The fat profile helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels and supports heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in niacin, thiamine and folate, peanuts aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They provide magnesium, phosphorus, iron and zinc, important for bones, blood and immune function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols and resveratrol in peanuts help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Nut and legume allergy
items.content: Peanuts are one of the most common allergens and can trigger severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of their fat content, peanuts are energy‑dense; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Added sugar in the glaze
items.content: Honey‑roasted varieties contain extra sugar, which may be unsuitable for diabetics or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Aflatoxin risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth producing aflatoxins; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Honey‑roasted peanuts are perfect as a snack, tossed into granola, yogurt, baked goods, or used in Asian dishes such as salads and noodle stir‑fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze to prevent fat oxidation.
